specification.problem: Quantum property testing of monotonicity of f:{0,1}^n->{0,1} with one-sided error: accept monotone f with certainty, reject eps-far f with bounded error, using Otilde(n^{1/4} eps^{-1/2}) queries. The abstract gives only the query complexity and the testing guarantee, not the algorithm.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Formalize the testing problem, the eps-farness definition, the claimed query bound, and a tiny explicit instance (n=2) with a phase-oracle query model. The paper's actual algorithm (e.g. how violating edges or pairs are found with quantum search) is outside scope and not reconstructed. The comparison with the randomized algorithm is also outside scope.

symbols.meaning: coordinatewise partial order, x_i<=y_i for all i
normalized Hamming distance between f and g

equations.label: Monotonicity
equations.latex: f\in\mathcal{M}\iff \forall x,y\in\{0,1\}^n:\ x\preceq y\Rightarrow f(x)\le f(y)
equations.description: Definition of a monotone Boolean function.
equations.justification: Standard definition of the property being tested; the abstract only names monotone functions.
assumptions: Coordinatewise partial order on the hypercube

equations.label: Epsilon-farness
equations.description: Standard definition of being eps-far from monotone.
equations.justification: The abstract uses eps-far without defining it; normalized Hamming distance is the standard convention.

equations.label: Testing guarantee
equations.description: Accept/reject behaviour of the tester. One-sided error is read from 'accepts a monotone function'; the 2/3 constant is the usual bounded-error choice.
equations.abstract_quote: accepts a monotone function, and rejects a function that is $\varepsilon$-far from being monotone
equations.justification: Inferred from the abstract's accept/reject statement with bounded error; the constant 2/3 is an assumption.
assumptions: Acceptance of monotone f is with certainty

equations.label: Query complexity
equations.description: Claimed number of quantum queries to f.

equations.label: Phase query oracle
equations.description: Standard quantum query access model for f.
equations.justification: The abstract says 'queries to a function'; this is the usual quantum oracle model, not stated in the abstract.
